FINAL OUTPUT CONTRACT: your ENTIRE final message must be exactly one bare JSON object (schema_version "1") - no code fence, no text before or after it. The Markdown answer lives only inside its reply_markdown string; each defect goes in findings[]. A prose final message cannot be ingested, however good the answer is.

Acceptance review of wave 24 (timeout continuation and partial salvage, per-purpose timeouts, -Range, F15-1, one truth about availability) at commit 65f5649, per the brief. Rule the open findings listed below as the brief says (only F02-9, F02-10, F02-11, F03-4, F03-5, F04-9, F04-10 are this wave's; mark the rest not-checked), then hunt for new defects in what wave 24 built, citing lines. Budget your time - a diff review of one wave. ACCEPT only if no blocker or major remains.

Read the brief at `.collab/companions-2026-09-26/handoffs/06-claude-wave24-acceptance.md` (path relative to the repository root, which is your working directory) and answer every numbered question in it.

Tools: you may read files of the repository (read_file); writing files, the shell and the web tools are disabled in this consultation (--disable-write --disable-shell --disable-web-tools) - do not try them; make NO file changes; a check that needs a command belongs under `## Requested checks`.

Review purpose: acceptance. Decide whether the result can be accepted. The verdict, the blockers, the unproven scenarios and an OBSERVABLE first-run checklist (what must be seen in logs or output on the first real run before an exit code 0 is believed) are mandatory.

Findings from earlier consultations in this task that are still open (id - status - locations - claim - trigger - verify):
- F02-1 - proposed - plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-scoreboard.ps1:171 - The additive score `1 + yes + 0.5*partly - no` with floor 0.25 is volume-sensitive and lets accumulated exposure dominate observed quality; the floor also maps every sufficiently bad history to the same value. - trigger: One lineage has many slightly positive ratings while another has one clean positive rating, or two lineages have several negative ratings. - verify: Construct synthetic histories with equal rates but different counts and compare the proposed score against a Beta-smoothed rate.
- F02-2 - proposed - plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-consult-common.ps1:4380, plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-findings.ps1:402, plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-scoreboard.ps1:119 - Ratings and consultation numbers are task-scoped, so joining cross-task telemetry by `n` alone can attach a rating to the wrong consultation and therefore the wrong topics or lineage. - trigger: Two task ledgers both contain consultation n=1 and routing aggregates every task as the design specifies. - verify: Create two temporary task ledgers with n=1 and different topics, rate one, then run a prototype aggregate and inspect attribution.
- F02-3 - proposed - plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-findings.ps1:416, plugins/codex-consult/skills/consult-codex/SKILL.md:293 - The 90-day window is undefined and re-rating can make old evidence look recent, while ratings are missing-not-at-random because the skill says structured responders are preferentially rated. - trigger: An old consultation is re-rated, or a prose/failed reviewer receives fewer ratings than a structured reviewer, before automated routing consumes the data. - verify: Re-rate a consultation older than 90 days and check whether a prototype score includes it based on `when` rather than consultation completion.
- F02-4 - proposed - plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-scoreboard.ps1:171 - Topic scoring is underspecified: normalization, deduplication, missing-topic fallback, multi-topic credit and the mean-of-means can double-count one judgment or dilute strong purpose evidence. - trigger: A consultation has topics `[security,tests]` and one rating, or a request has one topic with no ratings but purpose ratings exist. - verify: Feed one multi-topic rating through candidate formulas and compare its influence with a single-topic rating.
- F02-5 - proposed - plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-consult-common.ps1:4888 - Diversity-before-rank can deterministically displace a clearly superior second model of a large lab with a near-useless representative of a small lab. - trigger: Labs A has scores 10 and 9.5 and lab B has 0.25; the requested size is two. - verify: Run selection with the stated synthetic scores and assert whether the 9.5 candidate is excluded.
- F02-6 - proposed - plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-consult-common.ps1:4910, plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-consult.ps1:1221 - Panel-size semantics leave `none`/`chore`, `-PanelSize` combined with `-PanelAll`, overlarge sizes, and ordering of availability/weighty/routing filters undefined; implementations can count skipped or merely planned members differently. - trigger: `-Panel -Purpose chore -PanelSize 5`, or `-PanelAll -PanelSize 2`, with one unavailable and one weighty entry. - verify: Dry-run the listed combinations against a fake roster and compare runner counts and reasons.
- F02-7 - proposed - plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-consult.ps1:1237 - Seeding with the panel id cannot reproduce a draw as specified because the id is generated after selection and afresh for every invocation, including dry runs; no user-supplied seed exists. - trigger: Run the same dry run twice with identical inputs and expect the documented same-seed reproduction. - verify: Invoke identical fake dry runs twice and compare printed routing picks for equal inputs.
- F02-8 - proposed - plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-consult-common.ps1:4894 - The no-ratings fallback and `-PanelOrder roster` contract contradict themselves: equal-weight draws shuffle, yet the text also says no ratings means roster order, and it does not say whether exploration and diversity still apply. - trigger: A fresh repository has no ratings and runs a size-three panel twice. - verify: Specify and test a state table for `{no ratings, ratings} x {default, roster} x {diversity}` and compare expected orders.
- F02-9 - proposed - plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-consult-common.ps1:4503, plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-providers.ps1:252, plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-consult-hook.ps1:85 - A quota failure without a known reset is represented inconsistently: health already gives it a 60-minute Until, roster walks skip it, but provider rows and the hook only change availability for QuotaKnown, so they still report the endpoint available. - trigger: A 429 quota failure with no Retry-After occurs at 10:31 and SessionStart runs at 10:40. - verify: Seed a fake quota failure without retry_after and compare roster, provider, hook and explicit-run outcomes at +10 and +61 minutes.
- F02-10 - proposed - plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-providers.ps1:257, plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-consult-hook.ps1:85 - The hook cannot show availability per roster entry because codex-providers emits one row per provider label and records only the first roster position/model; multi-model labels collapse or disappear. - trigger: The roster has `gemini :: pro` and `gemini :: flash`, or two openai models, with one unavailable. - verify: Run `codex-providers.ps1 -Json -NoNetwork` with two models on one label and compare row count with roster entry count.
- F02-11 - proposed - plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-consult-common.ps1:4943 - Endpoint-group availability is ill-defined because Get-PanelPlan computes groups only from selected runners, while an outage must propagate across every roster entry sharing credentials or quota even when that entry is not selected. - trigger: Two agy labels share a Google quota but panel size one selects only a codex member, or required checks inspect an unselected agy entry. - verify: Build a roster with shared-fingerprint labels and one different selected runner, then compare group membership for availability and concurrency.
- F02-12 - proposed - plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-consult-common.ps1:4616, plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-consult-common.ps1:4635, plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-consult.ps1:1221 - `-Require` and roster `require` lack a complete contract and can silently proceed: required available members can lose their seats to size/diversity draws, matching and precedence are unspecified, and current fail-closed roster validation rejects the new keys. - trigger: Acceptance requires openai, but PanelSize 2 selects two higher-ranked members; or a roster adds `lab`/`require` without another schema change. - verify: Dry-run cases where a required available reviewer falls below the panel cap and where CLI and roster requirements conflict; assert exit 5 and no writes.
- F02-13 - proposed - plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-consult.ps1:2155, plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-consult.ps1:2157 - Role loading is unsafe and ambiguous: name validation, traversal, plugin-versus-repository precedence, exact insertion point relative to the output contract/schema, and `-Role`/`-Roles` conflict or count mismatch are unspecified; assigning roles to randomized pick order also makes member-role pairing nondeterministic. - trigger: A repository defines `.collab/roles/../../x.md`, shadows a built-in role, or passes more `-Roles` values than the panel size. - verify: Dry-run traversal, shadowing, mismatched role counts and repeated members with a fixed routing seed and inspect exact prompt/ledger output.
- F02-14 - proposed - tests/harness-panel.ps1:257, tests/harness-roster.ps1:415, .collab/companions-2026-09-26/handoffs/01-claude-companions-design.md:61 - The proposed fake-only test list omits high-risk boundaries: task-local n collisions, re-rating recency, rating bias/decay, topic fallback and multi-topic credit, lab normalization and quality gaps, size precedence, deterministic PRNG across PowerShell versions, unknown-reset transitions, shared endpoint outages, -Require pinning/precedence, role path safety and overflow behavior of the one-line hook. - trigger: Acceptance relies on the listed happy-path tests after implementation. - verify: Run the expanded deterministic harness matrix under both Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 and require exact outputs, not statistical pass criteria.
- F02-15 - proposed - README.md:1572 - The documented claim that findings repeat past about five diverse members has no repository evidence or measurement definition and can become an unjustified selection cap. - trigger: The README rule is used to size panels or stop adding reviewers. - verify: Measure marginal unique verified findings per added member over historical panels and report uncertainty before publishing a threshold.
- F03-1 - proposed - .collab/companions-2026-09-26/handoffs/01-claude-companions-design.md, plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-scoreboard.ps1:172, plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-findings.ps1:402 - The R15 score formula (1 + yes + 0.5*partly - no, floor 0.25) conflates rating volume with quality, and the all-purpose fallback inherits unrelated-purpose ratings plus the +1 baseline; ratings do record `when` (codex-findings.ps1:410) so the 90-day window is implementable, but the formula itself mis-ranks. - trigger: Two lineages on one purpose: 20 ratings at 80% yes vs 3 ratings at 100% yes - the former draws at roughly 17:3 odds despite the lower rate. - verify: Compute both formulas over the real findings.json ratings (RC1) and compare the resulting draw-weight ratios per lineage.
- F03-2 - proposed - .collab/companions-2026-09-26/handoffs/01-claude-companions-design.md, plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-consult-common.ps1:4540 - Diversity-before-rank guarantees a panel slot to a lab whose only representative sits at the 0.25 floor (rated all 'no'), displacing a strong second member of another lab; additionally the lab default (provider label) misfires for agy entries whose label is free text - one lab can occupy two 'labs' while sharing one quota. - trigger: Roster with labs A (two entries, scores 2.0 and 1.8) and B (one entry, score 0.25), panel size 2: B's 0.25 entry is picked over A's 1.8 entry. - verify: With fakes, construct the trigger roster and confirm the picked pair under the specified algorithm.
- F03-3 - proposed - .collab/companions-2026-09-26/handoffs/01-claude-companions-design.md - -Role <name> loads templates/role-<name>.md but the design never specifies name validation; 'unknown role refused' implies file-existence lookup, which without slug validation permits path traversal (-Role ../brief reads templates/../brief.md, and worse with .collab/roles/ roots). - trigger: -Role ../../some-file or -Role '..\x' on Windows. - verify: After implementation, run the bridge with -Role ../x against fakes and confirm refusal.
- F03-4 - proposed - plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-consult-hook.ps1:74 - The hook parses codex-providers verdicts with the regex ^(available|unavailable|unknown) - the addendum's new 'out - ... (until ...)' line and relative hints will not parse; the addendum never mentions updating the parser, so the sharpened line degrades to 'reviewer check failed'. - trigger: Any endpoint out with the new -Short output format. - verify: Run the hook against a ledger containing a fresh quota failure after the format change.
- F03-5 - proposed - plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-providers.ps1:252, plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-consult-common.ps1:4801 - Addendum item 9's 'quota without known reset marks the endpoint out for 60 minutes' already exists for the roster walk (Get-PreflightVerdict -RosterWalk refuses it, common.ps1:4801-4806); only the codex-providers display lags (lines 252/295 require QuotaKnown). - F03-6 - proposed - .collab/companions-2026-09-26/handoffs/01-claude-companions-design.md - Design item 6 contradicts itself - equal weights still shuffle, yet with no ratings the order is documented as roster order even though no ratings is exactly the equal-weights case - and it creates a discontinuity: the first rating recorded anywhere flips every panel from deterministic roster order to shuffled draws. - trigger: The first -Rate ever recorded in a repository. - verify: Fakes: run a panel before and after recording one rating; diff the picked order distribution.

Also, reproducibility only holds for a frozen eligible/score snapshot - new ratings change picks for the same seed; the routing record mitigates forensically but the test claim needs the caveat. - trigger: Replaying a recorded seed in a new process after GetHashCode-based seeding. - verify: Unit test: same panel id seeded in two separate pwsh processes must produce the same pick.
- F03-8 - proposed - .collab/companions-2026-09-26/handoffs/01-claude-companions-design.md - -Roles a,b,c assigns roles 'in order to the picked members', but picked order is now the seeded draw order, so role assignment is a lottery: an edge-cases or security role can land on the floor-scored member, which inverts the intent of giving narrow roles to suitable reviewers. - trigger: -Panel -Roles security,tests with a draw that picks the weakest member first. - verify: Fakes: two seeds, same roles; check which lineage receives the security role.
- F03-9 - proposed - plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-consult.ps1:1530 - -Require defines refusal BEFORE anything starts but not failure after start: today a member failing at launch is recorded skipped and the panel proceeds (exit 0 only when all usable, exit 1 otherwise, codex-consult.ps1:1530-1531). - F03-10 - proposed - plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-consult-common.ps1:4616 - The roster validator refuses unknown keys (common.ps1:4616 top level, 4635 per entry), so the design's lab field, require defaults, and ledger topics all need whitelist updates the design never lists; and a typo'd lineage in a require default silently never matches any entry, disabling the guard without error. - trigger: Roster gains "lab" before the validator is updated: every run refuses with 'unknown key'. - verify: Add a lab key to a test roster and load it at HEAD: expect refusal.
- F03-11 - proposed - plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-scoreboard.ps1:177 - Ratings store no topics; topic attribution depends on joining consult_id to the ledger's new topics[], but the scoreboard's fallback path (rating's own purpose field when n is not in the ledger, line 177-180) has no topic equivalent - older or pruned ledger entries silently lose topic attribution, and the design does not say where selection-time scoring lives, risking drift between the bridge's scoring and the scoreboard's -By topic aggregation. - trigger: -Topic on a consultation whose ledger entry is later unreadable: the rating counts for the purpose but not the topic. - verify: Rate a topic'd consultation, remove the ledger entry in a fake store, run -By topic.

- F04-1 - proposed - .collab/companions-2026-09-26/handoffs/01-claude-companions-design.md, plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-consult-common.ps1:4380 - R14 item 2 (deterministic: best-ranked per lab, then the rest by rank) and R15 item 6 (weighted random draw without replacement plus 0.2 exploration per slot) are two mutually exclusive selection rules, and the design never states how they compose, so the feature is unimplementable as written. - trigger: Any `-Panel` run once R14+R15 ship: the implementer must decide whether the lab pass runs before, inside or instead of the draw. - verify: Write the composition rule as pseudo-code and check one worked example: 2 labs (A: a1 score 3, a2 score 2; B: b1 score 1), k=2, seed that explores slot 2 — state which members run and whether the lab guarantee held.
- F04-2 - proposed - plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-consult-common.ps1:4380, plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-findings.ps1:402, .collab/companions-2026-09-26/handoffs/01-claude-companions-design.md - The brief's code fact invites a cross-task rating join by `n`, but `n` is unique only within a task and `Read-AllTaskConsults` flattens every task's consults and drops the task, so a repository-wide score joined on `n` mis-attributes ratings between tasks. - trigger: Two tasks each with a consult n=6, one rated `no` — the score of the unrelated reviewer on the other task's n=6 is polluted. - verify: Grep two different tasks' findings.json for the same rating `n` and confirm both exist, then confirm Read-AllTaskConsults returns both consults indistinguishably.

- F04-4 - proposed - .collab/companions-2026-09-26/handoffs/01-claude-companions-design.md, plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-findings.ps1:410 - The score formula (additive, floor 0.25, neutral 1) ranks a reviewer with one `no` below a reviewer that has never been rated, and its unbounded upper range collapses the weighted draw into near-deterministic top-pick selection. - trigger: Ratings [no] → 0.25 versus no ratings → 1.0; ratings [30×yes] → 31 versus [10×yes,1×no] → 10.5. - verify: Compute the score for [no], [yes,no], [] and [30×yes] and check the ordering against the intent that proven reviewers outrank untried ones.

1|<#
2|.SYNOPSIS
3|    SessionStart hook: one line saying which reviewers are out right now, and until when.
4|
5|.DESCRIPTION
6|    Runs at the start of a Claude Code session in any project where the plugin is
7|    enabled (hooks/hooks.json). Prints ONE line to stdout, which Claude Code adds to the
8|    agent's context (wave 24, D14-D17 - the line `codex-providers.ps1 -Short` prints):
9|
10|        codex-consult: out - openai :: gpt-6-astra (until Sun 20:35, in 2d 10h), gemini :: *
11|        (until Sun 21:30, in 2d 11h); 9 of 11 reviewers available
12|
13|    or `codex-consult: all 11 reviewers available`. Every roster entry is judged with the
14|    roster walk's own verdict (Select-PanelMembers -All: credentials, the launch invariant,
15|    the endpoint health of THIS repository's ledgers - an auth failure, a usage limit with a
16|    reset ahead, one without a reset for 60 minutes after it was hit); the entries of one
17|    endpoint group that share the state collapse to `<label> :: *`; reset times are LOCAL
18|    with a rounded relative hint; nothing is cut. An entry whose check needs the network (the
19|    agy engine's `agy models`) is `not checked` here - "..., 2 not checked" in the count -
20|    unless THIS repository's ledgers hold a usable reply on that endpoint from the last 60
21|    minutes (then it is available); a recorded auth failure or usage limit still shows it
22|    out. The muse engine's sign-in check reads ~/.config/muse/auth.json locally and runs here
23|    too, as does its billing guard (`meta :: <model> (refused: META_API_KEY is set)`).
24|    Without a roster: the providers of the Codex config ("... (no reviewer roster)").
25|
26|    When the Codex CLI is not on PATH: `codex-consult: codex CLI not found on PATH - follow
27|    the setup-providers skill`. Everything else (an unreadable config, an unusable roster, a
28|    crash inside the check) is reported in the same one-line form and never fails the
29|    session: the exit code is always 0. No network call, no lock, nothing written: it runs
30|    `codex-providers.ps1 -Short -Json -NoNetwork` and prints the `line` of its object.
31|
32|    Cost: about one second (`codex login status` for the built-in openai), once per
33|    session. Disable the hook by disabling the plugin's hooks in Claude Code settings.
34|
35|    Runs on Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7.
36|#>
37|[CmdletBinding()]
38|param(
39|    # Where consultations are stored (endpoint health is read from every task ledger
40|    # under it). Relative paths resolve against the git repo root of the current directory.
41|    [string]$CollabDir = '.collab'
42|)
43|
44|$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
45|$line = ''
46|try {
47|    $providers = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'codex-providers.ps1'
48|    $psExe = (Get-Process -Id $PID).Path
49|    $codex = Get-Command codex -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
50|    if (-not $codex) {
51|        $line = 'codex-consult: codex CLI not found on PATH - follow the setup-providers skill before consulting a reviewer'
52|    } else {
53|        $previous = $ErrorActionPreference
54|        $ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
55|        $raw = @(& $psExe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $providers -Short -Json -NoNetwork -CollabDir $CollabDir 2>&1 | ForEach-Object { "$_" })
56|        $code = $LASTEXITCODE
57|        $ErrorActionPreference = $previous
58|        $jsonStart = -1
59|        for ($i = 0; $i -lt $raw.Count; $i++) { if ($raw[$i] -match '^\s*\{') { $jsonStart = $i; break } }
60|        $obj = $null
61|        if ($jsonStart -ge 0) {
62|            try { $obj = (($raw[$jsonStart..($raw.Count - 1)]) -join "`n") | ConvertFrom-Json } catch { $obj = $null }
63|        }
64|        $text = $(if ($obj) { [string]$obj.line } else { '' })
65|        if ($text -match '^codex-consult: ' -and $text -notmatch "[`r`n]") {
66|            $line = $text
67|        } else {
68|            $first = (@($raw | Where-Object { $_ -and $_.Trim() }) | Select-Object -First 1)
69|            if (-not $first) { $first = "codex-providers.ps1 exited $code without output" }
70|            $line = "codex-consult: reviewer check failed - $first"
71|        }
72|    }
73|} catch {
74|    $msg = ("$($_.Exception.Message)" -replace '\s+', ' ').Trim()
75|    if ($msg.Length -gt 120) { $msg = $msg.Substring(0, 117) + '...' }
76|    $line = "codex-consult: reviewer check failed - $msg"
77|}
78|Write-Output $line
79|exit 0

1|# R14 + R15 + R16 - decisions after the design review (round 1)
2|
3|Reviews: 02 mimo :: mimo-v2.6-pro (ADVISE, F02-1..15), 03 kimi :: k3 (ADVISE, F03-1..12),
4|04 alibaba :: qwen3.8-max (ADVISE, F04-1..18). Panel 3 at once, 31 min wall. The design in 01
5|stands where not overridden here. The availability addendum (items 9-11) is implemented in the
6|"operator visibility" wave (wave 24) with the decisions D14-D17 below; the rest is the
7|companions wave.
8|
9|D1. One selection rule (F04-1, F02-5, F03-2, F04-3, F04-14). Eligible = available AND passes the
10|    weighty gate AND matches -Engine/-Model, computed once; ranking, the draw and exploration all
11|    use that one set. Fill slots 1..k by the weighted draw (D4). Diversity is a reserve, not a
12|    first pass: for the first min(k, number of labs with an entry scoring >= neutral) slots the
13|    draw is restricted to entries whose lab is not yet represented AND whose score is >= the
14|    neutral score; the remaining slots draw from the whole eligible rest. An entry below neutral
15|    never earns a lab seat. `lab` is NEVER defaulted to the provider label: a roster entry without
16|    `lab` gets its lab from a vendor table keyed on the model id prefix (qwen -> alibaba,
17|    deepseek -> deepseek, kimi/k3 -> moonshot, glm -> zhipu, dola/seed -> bytedance, mimo ->
18|    xiaomi, gemini -> google, muse -> meta, gpt -> openai); an unknown prefix = singleton lab
19|    (the entry's own lineage), with a run warning. Labs are canonicalised lowercase.
20|D2. Ratings and evidence keys (F02-2, F04-2, F03-11, F04-18). Ratings are keyed by `consult_id`
21|    (validated at -Rate time against the ledger entry's id; `n` kept for display) and copy
22|    `purpose`, `topics[]`, provider, model, engine and the consultation's `when` onto the rating
23|    record. Scoring reads the denormalised rating fields only - no join by `n` across tasks. The
24|    scoring function lives in `codex-consult-common.ps1` and is shared by the bridge and the
25|    scoreboard; the scoreboard reads findings.json of every task once per run (cached in memory).
26|D3. Score = a rate with a prior (F02-1, F03-1, F04-4, F02-3): for the ratings of the last 90 days
27|    (by the CONSULTATION's `when`, latest rating per consultation wins),
28|    `w = (yes + 0.5*partly + 2p) / (n + 4p)`, p = 0.5, then scaled into [0.25, 2] (w' = 0.25 +
29|    1.75*w). Hierarchy: the (lineage, purpose[, topic]) rate when it has >= 3 ratings, else the
30|    lineage's all-purpose rate (same formula), else neutral (w = 0.5 -> 1.125). Topics: canonical
31|    lowercase slugs, deduplicated; a rating credits each of its topics 1/t; a topic'd request
32|    averages weighted evidence (counts pooled), never a mean of means.
33|D4. The draw is exact and portable (F02-7, F04-5, F04-6, F03-7). Seed = SHA-256 of `task |
34|    purpose | brief_sha256 | sorted eligible lineages | nonce` where the nonce is `-PanelSeed <n>`
35|    when given (also `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_PANEL_SEED`), else the date (UTC, YYYY-MM-DD) - so a dry
36|    run and the real run of the same day print the same pick. Per slot: the first 8 bytes of
37|    SHA-256(seed || slot index) as a uniform in [0,1) times the remaining weight sum picks the
38|    winner, which is removed; exploration: with probability 0.2 (from the same uniform's next
39|    8 bytes) the slot draws uniformly from the same restricted pool. Byte-identical on Windows
40|    PowerShell 5.1 and pwsh 7 (a harness case asserts exact sequences for fixed seeds; a separate
41|    statistical case bounds the exploration rate over many seeds).
42|D5. Roster order stays the default until there is evidence (F02-8, F03-6). `-PanelOrder
43|    roster|routed` (default `routed`); in `routed` mode a lineage without >= 3 ratings on any
44|    purpose is scored neutral, and when NO eligible lineage has >= 3 ratings the run falls back
45|    to `roster` mode and records `routing.fallback: "no ratings"` (no shuffle without evidence).
46|    `roster` mode = today's order with size and eligibility only, no exploration.
47|D6. Panel size semantics (F02-6, F04-11, F04-17, F03-12). Defaults per purpose: chore 1, none 1,
48|    checkpoint 1, diff-review 2, framing 3, decision 3, core-contract 4, acceptance 4, stuck all.
49|    `-PanelSize` with `-PanelAll` refused. The size bounds members STARTED; the summary and the
50|    ledger `panel` record state `asked k, started j, usable i`; no backfill (documented).
51|    Third member state `not-picked` (reason `panel size k`), excluded from skip reporting. The
52|    floor warning (framing/decision with fewer than 2 members) goes into runWarnings and the
53|    ledger; suppressed when `-PanelSize` was given explicitly.
54|D7. `-Require` contract (F02-12, F04-7, F04-8, F03-9, F04-15, F03-10, F04-13). Matcher: a roster
55|    position `#5`, a bare provider label (every entry of it), or `provider :: model` with an
56|    optional ` [engine]` suffix, compared on the resolved identity (provider, model, engine) -
57|    never on display strings; a model-less entry is named by position or label. Required
58|    members are pinned BEFORE the draw fills the seats (they take seats first, the size counts
59|    them); evaluated with roster-walk availability semantics (a usage limit without a reset time
60|    is unavailable) on `-Panel` and on single `-Provider` runs alike; unavailable -> refused
61|    before anything starts, exit 5, dry run shows the same. Roster `require: { <purpose>:
62|    [matchers] }` validated at load: every matcher must resolve to an entry (else roster error).
63|    A required member failing AFTER start aborts the panel at the next slot boundary, exit 5, the
64|    ledger records the required set. Exit code 5 documented in the README table and the skill.
65|    The roster validator's allowlists gain `lab` (entry), `require` (top level).
66|D8. Roles (F02-13, F03-3, F03-8, F04-16). Role names are slugs (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,40}$`)
67|    validated before any path join; resolution: `.collab/roles/<name>.md` (repository) wins over
68|    the plugin's `templates/role-<name>.md`; `-Role` and `-Roles` are mutually exclusive; more
69|    roles than picked members is refused; `-Roles` assigns by SCORE RANK among the picked members
70|    (highest first), and a roster entry may carry `roles: [..]` it is willing to take (a role
71|    goes only to a willing entry when any is willing). The role block is inserted after the ask
72|    and before the brief, never inside the output contract. Ledger `role` per member.
73|D9. Tests to update (F04-12, F02-14): every assertion pinning roster order or "N of M would run"
74|    per purpose is listed in the brief and rewritten to the recorded `routing.picked`; fixed-seed
75|    exact sequences replace rate assertions; cases for task-local n collisions, re-rating recency,
76|    lab normalisation, quality gaps in diversity, size precedence, -Require pinning and matcher,
77|    role slug traversal, unknown-reset transitions, shared endpoint outages.
78|D10. Docs (F02-15): "about five" is labelled an operational heuristic; the scoreboard gains a
79|     column for unique findings per member so the claim can be measured later.
80|D11. Exploration and gates (F04-14): see D1 - one eligible set.
81|
82|Availability (implemented in wave 24, the operator visibility wave):
83|D14. One shared availability verdict (F02-9, F03-5): `Get-PreflightVerdict -RosterWalk` semantics
84|     are the truth for every surface - the roster walk, `codex-providers.ps1` rows, `-Short` and
85|     the hook; a quota without a known reset reads "out (limit hit <t>, reset unknown; retry
86|     after <t+60 min>)" everywhere (today only the walk refuses it; the display lags).
87|D15. Per-entry availability records (F02-10, F04-9): `Select-PanelMembers` gains `-NoNetwork`
88|     (passed to its preflight) and the hook/listing build their lines from its full member list
89|     (every entry judged, not the first available one); one clause per endpoint group when all
90|     of the group share the state, else per entry.
91|D16. Endpoint groups over ALL resolved roster identities (F02-11): the credential/quota group map
92|     is computed from every roster entry (not from the selected runners), and an outage marks the
93|     whole group.
94|D17. The line itself (F04-10, F03-4): no per-reason truncation in the short form; three counts
95|     (`available / out / not checked`); reset times converted with ToLocalTime() and a rounded
96|     relative hint; the hook's parser is updated in the same wave (or `-Short` gets a JSON mode
97|     the hook reads).

4|
5|.DESCRIPTION
6|    Runs at the start of a Claude Code session in any project where the plugin is
7|    enabled (hooks/hooks.json). Prints ONE line to stdout, which Claude Code adds to the
8|    agent's context (wave 24, D14-D17 - the line `codex-providers.ps1 -Short` prints):
9|
10|        codex-consult: out - openai :: gpt-6-astra (until Sun 20:35, in 2d 10h), gemini :: *
11|        (until Sun 21:30, in 2d 11h); 9 of 11 reviewers available
12|
13|    or `codex-consult: all 11 reviewers available`. Every roster entry is judged with the
14|    roster walk's own verdict (Select-PanelMembers -All: credentials, the launch invariant,
15|    the endpoint health of THIS repository's ledgers - an auth failure, a usage limit with a
16|    reset ahead, one without a reset for 60 minutes after it was hit); the entries of one
17|    endpoint group that share the state collapse to `<label> :: *`; reset times are LOCAL
18|    with a rounded relative hint; nothing is cut. An entry whose check needs the network (the
19|    agy engine's `agy models`) is `not checked` here - "..., 2 not checked" in the count -
20|    unless THIS repository's ledgers hold a usable reply on that endpoint from the last 60
21|    minutes (then it is available); a recorded auth failure or usage limit still shows it
22|    out. The muse engine's sign-in check reads ~/.config/muse/auth.json locally and runs here
23|    too, as does its billing guard (`meta :: <model> (refused: META_API_KEY is set)`).
24|    Without a roster: the providers of the Codex config ("... (no reviewer roster)").
25|
26|    When the Codex CLI is not on PATH: `codex-consult: codex CLI not found on PATH - follow
27|    the setup-providers skill`. Everything else (an unreadable config, an unusable roster, a
28|    crash inside the check) is reported in the same one-line form and never fails the
29|    session: the exit code is always 0. No network call, no lock, nothing written: it runs
30|    `codex-providers.ps1 -Short -Json -NoNetwork` and prints the `line` of its object.
31|
32|    Cost: about one second (`codex login status` for the built-in openai), once per
33|    session. Disable the hook by disabling the plugin's hooks in Claude Code settings.
34|
35|    Runs on Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7.
36|#>
37|[CmdletBinding()]
38|param(
39|    # Where consultations are stored (endpoint health is read from every task ledger
40|    # under it). Relative paths resolve against the git repo root of the current directory.
41|    [string]$CollabDir = '.collab'
42|)
43|
44|$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
45|$line = ''
46|try {
47|    $providers = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'codex-providers.ps1'
48|    $psExe = (Get-Process -Id $PID).Path
49|    $codex = Get-Command codex -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
50|    if (-not $codex) {
51|        $line = 'codex-consult: codex CLI not found on PATH - follow the setup-providers skill before consulting a reviewer'
52|    } else {
53|        $previous = $ErrorActionPreference
54|        $ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
55|        $raw = @(& $psExe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $providers -Short -Json -NoNetwork -CollabDir $CollabDir 2>&1 | ForEach-Object { "$_" })
56|        $code = $LASTEXITCODE
57|        $ErrorActionPreference = $previous
58|        $jsonStart = -1
59|        for ($i = 0; $i -lt $raw.Count; $i++) { if ($raw[$i] -match '^\s*\{') { $jsonStart = $i; break } }
60|        $obj = $null
61|        if ($jsonStart -ge 0) {
62|            try { $obj = (($raw[$jsonStart..($raw.Count - 1)]) -join "`n") | ConvertFrom-Json } catch { $obj = $null }
63|        }
64|        $text = $(if ($obj) { [string]$obj.line } else { '' })
65|        if ($text -match '^codex-consult: ' -and $text -notmatch "[`r`n]") {
66|            $line = $text
67|        } else {
68|            $first = (@($raw | Where-Object { $_ -and $_.Trim() }) | Select-Object -First 1)
69|            if (-not $first) { $first = "codex-providers.ps1 exited $code without output" }
70|            $line = "codex-consult: reviewer check failed - $first"
71|        }
72|    }
73|} catch {
74|    $msg = ("$($_.Exception.Message)" -replace '\s+', ' ').Trim()
75|    if ($msg.Length -gt 120) { $msg = $msg.Substring(0, 117) + '...' }
76|    $line = "codex-consult: reviewer check failed - $msg"
77|}
78|Write-Output $line
79|exit 0
